description: Cold, fear, music: shivers have several causes. They all pass through the nervous system, but not for the same reasons.

hero.hook: A shiver of cold and a shiver of music do not tell the same story.

blocks.text: You shiver as you go out into the rain. You also shiver when hearing a song that upsets you. Same word, different mechanisms.
In both cases, the body reacts quickly. But one is mainly used to warm up, the other is more about pleasure and emotions.
The body wants to stay around **37 °C**. When the skin detects cold, it alerts an area of ​​the brain, the **hypothalamus**, which acts like a thermostat.

blocks.caption: Goosebumps: an old reflex to raise the hackles.

blocks.text: The muscles contract very quickly and repeatedly: this is the shiver. These contractions produce heat. “Goosebumps” comes from an old reflex: raising the hairs to better insulate. At home, with little fur, it mainly serves as a vestige.

sections.title: The thrill of the cold: a mini-boiler

blocks.text: Faced with a threat, the [[The sympathetic nervous system]] (the “alert” branch of the nervous system) is activated. It releases **adrenaline**. The muscles tense, the heart races, the skin may shiver.

blocks.caption: Adrenaline prepares the body to react quickly.

blocks.text: This same system explains why you can get goosebumps while watching a horror movie... while you're cozy on your couch.
Certain thrills, sometimes called “chills”, arrive with a strong emotion: music, speech, film. They activate the brain's **rewards** circuit, with **dopamine**, a substance linked to pleasure.
This is not useful for immediate survival. Rather, it is the body that reacts to an intense emotion, like a passing wave.

Chills with high fever can signal an infection. Constant chills for no clear reason merit medical attention. But most of the time, a shiver from cold, stress, or music is simply the body doing its job.
Cold shivers produce heat. Those of fear prepare to react. Those of music touch on emotional pleasure. Same feeling, different causes.
